title: Host and guest
description: Is this one machine OK? Pick a host or guest from inventory/lab.yaml. Open it from a HostUnreachable, HttpProbeFailed, PveGuest* or TargetDown alert: ping, health URL, scrapes, Proxmox state, backup, resources and logs.

panels.title: Ping
panels.description: ICMP echo from the monitoring CT (rule HostUnreachable: no answer for 3 minutes; severity from the host's tier). DOWN means the host is off, unplugged or cut off from the network: check the Proxmox state tile next.

panels.title: Health URL
panels.description: The host's `health:` URL from inventory/lab.yaml, probed over HTTP (rule HttpProbeFailed: failing for 5 minutes; 2xx, or any answer for http_any). UP with Ping UP but this DOWN means the machine is alive and the service is not. n/a means the host has no health URL.

panels.title: Scrapes
panels.description: Every Prometheus scrape of this host, all jobs (node_exporter, probes, the Proxmox exporter, app /metrics): UP only when all succeed (rule TargetDown: a scrape failing for 5 minutes). The scrape table below names the failing job.

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Critical and warning alerts firing for this host or guest, whichever label they carry (host alerts by instance, guest alerts by Proxmox name, node alerts by node id). Info alerts are in the table below but not counted. Red means something here needs you.

targets.expr: (count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity=~"critical|warning", instance=~"$instance", id!~"(lxc|qemu)/.*|node/.*"}) or vector(0)) + (count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity=~"critical|warning", name=~"$instance", id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) or vector(0)) + (count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity=~"critical|warning", id=~"node/$instance"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Proxmox state
panels.description: A guest's run state from the Proxmox API (rule PveGuestDown: a guest with onboot=1 that is not running for 5 minutes), or whether the cluster sees a node online. OFF = stopped and not set to start on boot (the on-demand `ai` VM, the archive CT): by design, no alert. The router and switch are not Proxmox objects and show n/a.

targets.expr: (((pve_up{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left () pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"}) == 0) and on (id) (pve_onboot_status == 0)) + 2 or (pve_up{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left () pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"}) or pve_up{id=~"node/$instance"}

panels.title: Backup
panels.description: Whether the guest is in a backup job (rule PveGuestNotBackedUp: in none for an hour). Coverage only: a failed nightly run is not visible here, it arrives as a Proxmox notification. The PBS guest itself is excluded by the rule and shows n/a, like everything that is not a guest.

targets.expr: ((pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"} * 0 + 1) unless on (id) (pve_not_backed_up_info == 1) unless on (id) pve_guest_info{name="pbs"}) or ((pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"} * 0) and on (id) (pve_not_backed_up_info == 1) unless on (id) pve_guest_info{name="pbs"})

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the guest (or node) started, from the Proxmox API. A short uptime with no maintenance behind it is a reboot to explain; 'stopped' is a guest that is off. The Nodes board has the node_exporter view of boots.

targets.expr: ((pve_uptime_seconds{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left () pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"}) or pve_uptime_seconds{id=~"node/$instance"})

panels.title: Alerts for this host
panels.description: Every alert firing for the selected host or guest, all severities (the tile counts critical and warning only). Empty is the good state. Detail is the systemd unit or the guest name where the alert has one. The runbook for each is docs/runbooks/alerts.md under the alert's name.

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Every Prometheus target of this host: one row per job and port. Up is the scrape result (rule TargetDown). A DOWN row names the job to look at: node = node_exporter, blackbox_* = a probe of the host, pve = the Proxmox exporter, service/service_dmz = an app's /metrics.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU use as a share of the cores the guest is allotted (a 4-core VM at 50 % is using 2 cores), from the Proxmox API; for a node, of all its cores. Pinned near 100 % means the guest wants more cores than it has. For the monitoring CT this is the real figure: its node_exporter shows pve2's CPU. No alert rule.

targets.expr: (pve_cpu_usage_ratio{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left () pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"}) or pve_cpu_usage_ratio{id=~"node/$instance"}

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Memory the guest uses and the memory it is allotted, from the Proxmox API. For a container, used is its cgroup usage: touching the allotment means OOM kills. For a VM, used is the QEMU process's footprint on the node, which sits at the allotment after a few days because the guest's page cache fills it (a k3s VM reads about 100 %): its real use is Memory available in the node_exporter row (rule HostMemoryLow). A stopped guest reads 0 used.

panels.title: Disk
panels.description: Root disk used and its size, from the Proxmox API. Containers report it; QEMU guests read 0 used because there is no guest agent, so use the filesystem panel in the node_exporter row for the VMs. For a node it is its root filesystem. No alert rule: HostFilesystemFull works from node_exporter, not from this.

targets.expr: (pve_disk_size_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left () pve_guest_info{name=~"$instance", template="0"}) or pve_disk_size_bytes{id=~"node/$instance"}

panels.title: Disk I/O
panels.description: Bytes per second the guest reads from and writes to its disks, from the Proxmox API (no data for nodes). Heavy writes by one guest show up as busy time and latency on its node's disk: compare the Nodes board's Disk I/O row. No alert rule.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Bytes per second the guest receives and sends on its virtual NIC, from the Proxmox API (no data for nodes; the Nodes board has the physical NIC). A flat zero on a running guest is a dead interface. No alert rule.

panels.title: Ping round-trip
panels.description: Round-trip time of the ping from the monitoring CT. On the LAN it is sub-millisecond to a few milliseconds; a rise with no load behind it is a network or host problem. A gap is a lost ping (rule HostUnreachable fires after 3 minutes of them).

panels.title: Health URL timing
panels.description: Where the health URL's time goes: name lookup, TCP connect, TLS handshake, server processing and transfer (the phases add up to the probe's duration). A long processing slice is a slow service; a long connect or tls slice is the network or the host. Empty when the host has no health URL (rule HttpProbeFailed).

panels.title: Probe results over time
panels.description: When each probe failed, over the selected range: green = answered, red = failed. Ping red with health URL red is the host; only the health URL red is the service. The alerts fire after 3 minutes (HostUnreachable) and 5 minutes (HttpProbeFailed) of red.

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over the cores, from the host's own node_exporter (iowait and steal count as busy). Empty for hosts without one: only the Proxmox nodes, the monitoring CT and the k3s VMs have it. For the monitoring CT this line is pve2's, not the CT's; use the CPU panel above.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable / MemTotal from the host's own node_exporter. The dashed line is the HostMemoryLow threshold (10 %, held 15 minutes). Empty for hosts without a node_exporter.

panels.title: Filesystem free
panels.description: Free-space ratio of each mount from the host's own node_exporter. The dashed line is the HostFilesystemFull threshold (15 %, held 15 minutes). This is the disk figure for a VM, which the Proxmox view cannot give. Empty for hosts without a node_exporter.

panels.title: Logs
panels.description: Recent log lines of the selected host from VictoriaLogs, newest first: the journald host name, or a `hostname` label that starts with the name. Read it around the time a probe or scrape went red. Nothing here for devices that do not ship logs. Not checked by the generator's live verification.
